name: Cabinet
description: A lightweight self-hosted file cabinet and document manager.
summary: Cabinet v0.4.3 (released 2026-04-30) is the latest stable release, fixing a DMG signing regression present since v0.3.4 by correcting hardened-runtime entitlements for native modules. The landmark v0.4.0 release (433 commits) introduced a Skills system (installable agent skills in Anthropic format), a multi-provider BYOAI runtime supporting 8 CLI providers (Claude, Codex, Gemini, etc.), persistent terminal/PTY mode, a rebuilt Tasks Board with drag-and-drop, and a Cmd+K search palette backed by FlexSearch. The project also added MIT licensing, anonymous opt-out telemetry, and numerous UX and accessibility improvements. See the full changelog at https://github.com/hilash/cabinet.

answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in April 2026, including several same-day patch releases
answers.Does it support user authentication?: Not explicitly mentioned; a legal/disclaimer acceptance flow is present, but no user auth system is described

alternatives.name: Paperless-ngx
alternatives.review: Paperless-ngx offers far more powerful document indexing and OCR capabilities but is significantly heavier and more complex to set up than Cabinet.

alternatives.name: Teedy
alternatives.review: Teedy provides a more feature-rich document management system with user roles and workflows, but at the cost of greater resource consumption compared to Cabinet.

alternatives.name: Filestash
alternatives.review: Filestash excels as a universal file browser supporting many storage backends, but lacks the document-centric organization features that Cabinet focuses on.

alternatives.name: Docspell
alternatives.review: Docspell offers robust automated document processing and tagging with OCR, making it more powerful but considerably harder to configure than Cabinet.

alternatives.name: Nextcloud
alternatives.review: Nextcloud is a comprehensive cloud platform that includes file management and document handling, but it is far more expansive and resource-intensive than the minimal footprint Cabinet aims for.
